items.title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly in Cybersecurity – Week 29
items.feed_description: Authorities sanction Russian-based cybercriminals, attackers deploy Starland malware, and 300 imposter GitHub repos push BoryptGrab infostealer.
items.summary: SentinelOne highlights recent cybersecurity developments, including EU/UK sanctions against Russian cybercriminals and state-sponsored actors, U.S. sanctions on ransomware enablers, and the dismantling of bulletproof hosting infrastructure. A financially-motivated Russian threat group (UAT-11795) is exploiting trojanized remote tools to deploy Starland malware for data theft and ransomware. Over 300 imposter GitHub repositories are distributing BoryptGrab malware to steal sensitive data from developers. These incidents underscore evolving tactics in ransomware, supply chain attacks, and social engineering.
features: Starland malware with persistence, data exfiltration, and multi-platform capabilities (64-bit/32-bit shellcode chains)
BoryptGrab malware via GitHub impersonation, targeting 19 browsers and 32 crypto wallets
Redundant C2 communications using Polygon smart contracts and Telegram bots
Sanctions against Russian GRU/FSB-linked entities and ransomware infrastructure providers
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must prioritize detecting trojanized software distribution, monitoring for GitHub impersonation campaigns, and mitigating ransomware infrastructure ties. Organizations should enforce software verification processes and enhance endpoint detection for memory-resident malware like BoryptGrab.

items.title: Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy
items.feed_description: A technical analysis of three chained zero-day vulnerabilities in Siemens ROX II OT switches that allow privilege escalation and persistent root access. The post Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy appeared first on Unit 42 .
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers, in collaboration with Siemens, discovered three zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-40947, CVE-2025-40948, CVE-2025-40949) in Siemens ROX II OT switches that enable privilege escalation, root access, and persistent code execution. The vulnerabilities allow attackers to compromise industrial control networks through chained exploitation. Siemens recommends updating to firmware V2.17.1 to address these issues.
features: Three zero-day vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-40947, CVE-2025-40948, CVE-2025-40949) in Siemens ROX II OT switches
Exploit chain stages: arbitrary file disclosure, command injection, and task scheduler persistence
Firmware update V2.17.1 provided by Siemens as a mitigation
Palo Alto Networks NGFW with Advanced Threat Prevention virtual patching signatures for detection
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must prioritize updating OT infrastructure to prevent exploitation of these critical vulnerabilities, which could grant full control over industrial networks. Organizations should monitor for signs of command injection and persistent processes in OT environments.

items.title: AI Security Is Never Finished: Building the Continuous Red Teaming Loop
items.feed_description: Security programs are built around moments of closure: the finding is closed, the control passed, and the release can move forward. AI security refuses to cooperate with that model. A passing test is useful evidence, but only for a specific system, configuration, and moment. Production AI keeps moving. Models change behavior, prompts are revised, retrieval sources are added, agents gain tools, and users introduce unexpected context. Attackers adapt just as quickly. Yesterday’s clean result may not describe tomorrow’s risk. That has been the practical case for continuous AI red teaming. Now, research from the National Institute of Standards and Technology […] The post AI Security Is Never Finished: Building the Continuous Red Teaming Loop appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point highlights the limitations of static AI security testing, emphasizing that continuous red teaming is essential due to evolving AI behaviors and adversarial tactics. Research from NIST supports this by showing no finite guardrails can universally protect against adversarial prompts. The company outlines a continuous security loop combining adversarial discovery, hardening, and operational resilience to address AI risks dynamically.
features: Continuous adversarial discovery for identifying attack paths
Continuous hardening to refine policies and controls
Operational resilience for limiting exploit impact
Check Point AI Defense Plane integrating discovery, protection, governance, and assurance
Feedback loop for testing, monitoring, and production protection
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must adopt ongoing adversarial testing and adaptive defenses to counter evolving AI threats, ensuring systems remain secure as models and attack vectors evolve.

items.title: TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development
items.feed_description: TuxBot v3 Evolution, an IoT botnet framework built with LLMs. Read our analysis of its cross-compiled binaries, C2 architecture and bugs. The post TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development appeared first on Unit 42 .
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers uncovered TuxBot v3, a modular IoT botnet framework leveraging LLM-assisted development with cross-architecture compilation, a Go-based C2 server, and DDoS capabilities. The framework includes exploit code for 30+ IoT devices, fallback C2 mechanisms like DGA and P2P gossip, and a functional Telnet brute-force scanner. Researchers identified critical bugs in LLM-generated code and a XOR key decryption flaw affecting 9 entries in the string table.
features: Cross-compiled C bot agent for 17 architectures (ARM, MIPS, x86_64, etc.)
Go-based C2 server with DDoS-for-hire panel and SSH admin interface
Custom exploit VM and Docker-based test infrastructure
Telnet brute-force with 1,496 credential pairs
SHA512 DGA and Ed25519-signed P2P gossip fallback C2
XOR key decryption bug affecting 9 string table entries
Git log timeline showing Iranian-hosted development
Connection to Keksec/Kaitori infrastructure via IP 185.10.68.127
items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams must enhance IoT device protection against LLM-assisted botnets with cross-architecture capabilities. The XOR key decryption flaw and persistent DDoS infrastructure highlight the need for advanced endpoint detection, behavioral analysis, and real-time threat intelligence to mitigate evolving IoT botnet threats.

items.title: AI Agents are Only As Effective as Their Harness
items.feed_description: Every AI vendor is talking about agents – autonomous systems that handle complex tasks without constant human input. The promise is real. But one question gets asked too rarely: what makes an agent reliable enough to trust with your network security? The answer isn’t the model. It’s the harness. Agents Run on LLMs. Reliability Runs on Something Else AI agents get their reasoning power from large language models (LLMs). LLMs are impressive. They understand context, reason through complex problems, and plan across a wide range of tasks. But on its own, an LLM is a generalist. It knows a little about everything and not enough about your […] The post AI Agents are Only As Effective as Their Harness appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point emphasizes that AI agents' reliability in network security depends on their 'harness'—a framework combining skills, tools, and context. The company highlights its agentic platform built on these principles, leveraging 30 years of deployment experience and a proprietary Network Knowledge Graph for real-time environment awareness. This approach addresses hallucination risks by grounding AI decisions in dynamic, production-specific data rather than static models.
features: Three-core harness components: skills, tools, and context

Skills derived from 30 years of real-world deployment expertise
Dynamic context integration with security policies and regulations

items.why_it_matters: Endpoint security teams benefit from reduced hallucination risks and more reliable AI-driven decisions through Check Point's harness framework, enabling accurate threat detection and response in complex, production environments.

What was once a human-centric communication channel is quickly becoming an AI-driven workflow, and that shift introduces a new and largely unprotected attack surface. Much of the industry’s recent attention has centered […] The post Email Agent Hijacking: The Hidden Threat That Breaks Post-Delivery Security appeared first on Check Point Blog .
items.summary: Check Point identifies 'Email Agent Hijacking' as a new threat where malicious content manipulates AI agents' interpretation or outputs before human interaction. AI agents process emails pre-delivery, creating an unprotected attack surface. Post-delivery controls are ineffective against immediate AI actions. Organizations require preventive protections for AI-consumed content and validation of AI-generated responses.

items.title: Falcon Cloud Security June 2026 Release: Updates for Azure and Google Cloud
items.summary: CrowdStrike Falcon Cloud Security June 2026 release introduces enhanced Azure and Google Cloud security capabilities, including identity and permission visibility, exposed resource detection, and sensitive data protection. The update also integrates Falcon AIDR for threat detection in Kubernetes AI applications.
features: Enhanced visibility into Azure and Google Cloud identities and permissions
Detection of exposed cloud resources and misconfigurations
Protection of sensitive data across cloud environments
Falcon AIDR integration for threat detection in Kubernetes AI applications
items.why_it_matters: These updates strengthen security teams' ability to monitor and protect cloud infrastructure, reducing risks from misconfigurations and advanced threats in hybrid cloud environments.

items.title: The Identity Problem Hiding in AI Agent Deployments
items.summary: CrowdStrike highlights the identity problem in AI agent deployments, where OAuth tokens often mask the true requester, creating security risks. The blog emphasizes the need for stronger authentication mechanisms beyond basic OAuth to ensure proper identity verification in AI agent interactions.
features: Announced 'Continuous Identity for AI Agents' to address identity gaps in AI deployments
Integration with OpenID and IDPro for enhanced identity verification
Focus on securing AI agent interactions through robust authentication
items.why_it_matters: Without proper identity validation, AI agents could be exploited for unauthorized access, data exfiltration, or impersonation. CrowdStrike's updates aim to help security teams mitigate these risks by ensuring AI agents operate with verified identities.

items.title: 94% of Organizations Report Cloud Breaches: CrowdStrike State of CDR Survey
items.summary: CrowdStrike's State of CDR Survey highlights that 94% of organizations reported cloud breaches in 2023, driven by poor cloud visibility, inability to distinguish legitimate vs. malicious activity, and fragmented detection/response capabilities.
